Question:
# ALS evidence packet — draft v1

This curated input is not a comprehensive review. Every method receives the same UTF-8 file. Summaries are original paraphrases. Bibliographic metadata and abstracts were checked through the public NCBI ID converter and PubMed EFetch on 2026-10-05. Selected studies predate 2025; this does not remove knowledge already in a model's training. Co-Scientist outputs are not included.

## Research question

Propose one specific, testable hypothesis connecting phosphorylation of a nuclear-pore-complex nucleoporin to ALS-related neuronal dysfunction. Explain the causal chain, distinguish an initiating mechanism from a downstream response, and propose an experimental strategy that discriminates the hypothesis from an alternative. Identify supported premises, speculative bridges, and a falsifying observation. This adapts Co-Scientist Supplementary Note 10; nucleoporin phosphorylation is not supplied as an established ALS cause.

## S1 — TDP-43 and nuclear-pore dysfunction

Chou et al. (2018), *TDP-43 pathology disrupts nuclear pore complexes and nucleocytoplasmic transport in ALS/FTD*. Nature Neuroscience. DOI: `10.1038/s41593-017-0047-3`; PMID: `29311743`; PMCID: `PMC5800968`. [Primary record](https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/29311743/).

Nuclear-pore and transport components were associated with insoluble TDP-43 aggregates. Disease-linked TDP-43 disrupted nucleoporin localization and nuclear transport in experimental cell systems; relevant pore pathology was observed in ALS tissue. This supports examining the connection between TDP-43 pathology and transport disruption. It does not identify a nucleoporin phosphorylation event as the initiating cause or establish the same sequence in every ALS subtype.

## S2 — C9orf72-associated transport defects

Zhang et al. (2015), *The C9orf72 repeat expansion disrupts nucleocytoplasmic transport*. Nature. DOI: `10.1038/nature14973`; PMID: `26308891`; PMCID: `PMC4800742`. [Primary record](https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/26308891/).

Expanded C9orf72 repeat RNA was linked to altered RanGAP localization and impaired nuclear import in models and patient-derived neurons. Manipulations of transport or repeat-RNA-associated mechanisms modified model phenotypes. This supplies a genetic-context-specific route to transport dysfunction. It does not show that sporadic ALS arises by the same route or directly establish a nucleoporin phosphorylation mechanism.

## S3 — A stress-granule-independent route

Gasset-Rosa et al. (2019), *Cytoplasmic TDP-43 De-mixing Independent of Stress Granules Drives Inhibition of Nuclear Import, Loss of Nuclear TDP-43, and Cell Death*. Neuron. DOI: `10.1016/j.neuron.2019.02.038`; PMID: `30853299`; PMCID: `PMC6548321`. [Primary record](https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/30853299/).

Persistent cytoplasmic TDP-43 assemblies could form independently of conventional stress granules. They recruited or mislocalized transport-associated proteins and were associated with impaired transport, nuclear TDP-43 depletion, and cell death. Phosphorylated TDP-43 accumulated in these assemblies. That is not itself evidence of nucleoporin phosphorylation. The experimental perturbations do not establish that every physiological ALS trajectory begins in this way.

## S4 — A stress-granule-associated route

Zhang et al. (2018), *Stress Granule Assembly Disrupts Nucleocytoplasmic Transport*. Cell. DOI: `10.1016/j.cell.2018.03.025`; PMID: `29628143`; PMCID: `PMC6083872`. [Primary record](https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/29628143/).

Cellular stress recruited transport factors into stress granules and impaired nucleocytoplasmic transport. Altering stress-granule assembly modified transport defects and disease-model phenotypes. This provides a sequestration-based alternative to an intrinsic pore-modification hypothesis. Read alongside S3, it does not justify assuming that conventional stress granules are required for every TDP-43-associated transport defect.

## Evidence boundaries

- These selected passages do not establish that nucleoporin phosphorylation initiates ALS. Label a proposed kinase, modification site, or interaction as an assumption unless a supplied source supports it.
- Specify the ALS context; do not assume a universal mechanism across genetic and sporadic disease.
- Distinguish pore alteration, transport-factor sequestration, and failure secondary to broader stress.
- Explain temporal and perturbational evidence that would distinguish cause from consequence.
- Propose a research hypothesis rather than claiming a mechanism or treatment has been validated.


Title: Stress-activated phosphorylation of the FG-nucleoporin Nup98 initiates selective nuclear import failure upstream of TDP-43 mislocalization in TDP-43-proteinopathy motor neurons.

Hypothesis. In sporadic ALS motor neurons with TDP-43 proteinopathy, sustained stress activates a kinase that phosphorylates Nup98 at FG/GLFG-region sites, weakening the NPC permeability barrier and the rate of facilitated NLS-cargo import. This initiating pore modification reduces nuclear retention and import of TDP-43; cytoplasmic TDP-43 de-mixing, stress-granule-driven sequestration of transport factors, Ran-gradient collapse, and cell death are downstream amplifiers, not the first cause. C9orf72-initiated disease (S2 context) is excluded from scope, though convergence is permitted.

Supported premises (packet only). S1: NPC/transport disruption accompanies TDP-43 pathology in ALS tissue and experimental systems; co-occurrence, not direction. S3: stress-granule-independent cytoplasmic TDP-43 assemblies impair import, deplete nuclear TDP-43, and recruit/mislocalize transport proteins — the downstream arm. S4: SG assembly sequesters transport factors and impairs transport — both the sequestration alternative and the reason a phospho-null cannot be predicted to fully preserve import, since SGs independently impair transport. S2: transport dysfunction in the C9 genetic context only.

Assumptions (no packet support). A1: a stress-activated kinase (p38/JNK as candidates) phosphorylates Nup98 in adult motor neurons. A2: candidate residues are 2–3 clustered Ser/Thr sites in/near GLFG repeats and adjacent linkers, nominated a priori from mitotic Nup98 phospho-mapping; this sourcing is unverified prior knowledge and analogy, to be re-confirmed by MS before use. A3: the directional claim that phosphorylation precedes TDP-43 egress, inverted from S1's co-occurrence. A4: specificity to TDP-43-proteinopathy ALS. Asp/Glu phosphomimetic substitutions are acknowledged as chemically poor phosphate mimics and will anchor no conclusion.

Causal chain (revised). Initiating: kinase activation → Nup98 FG phosphorylation → increased passive permeability and reduced facilitated NLS-import at the pore. Secondary: reduced nuclear TDP-43 retention → cytoplasmic de-mixing (S3) → SG formation and transport-factor sequestration (S4) → Ran-gradient dissipation → cell death. Ran gradient is deliberately decoupled from the initiating lesion: RanGAP/RCC1 localization primarily maintain it, so gradient changes are used as downstream readouts, not bundled into the initiation claim.

Alternative explanations. (1) Sequestration-first: SGs or TDP-43 assemblies deplete soluble import machinery; phosphorylation is absent or irrelevant. (2) Physical displacement: insoluble TDP-43 directly distorts pores (consistent with S1), phosphorylation a bystander. (3) Genetic route: C9orf72 repeat RNA/DPR mechanisms (S2). (4) Reverse causality: late phosphorylation secondary to stress or disassembly.

Discriminating strategy.
• Modification validation first: knock in endogenous tagged Nup98; map phosphorylation sites by MS of purified nuclear-envelope fractions across a stress time course; validate phosphopeptide-specific antibodies against mapped sites, or use chemically inducible kinase recruitment to tagged Nup98 for acute, reversible gain-of-function — this replaces reliance on Asp/Glu phosphomimetics, which remain secondary only.
• Direct attribution: digitonin-permeabilized neurons reconstituted with recombinant phosphorylated versus phospho-null Nup98 (FG-region constructs MS-verified) to measure passive tracer flux and NLS-import kinetics directly attributable to the modification, separating pore effects from import-factor or Ran effects.
• Temporal tests: (i) stress-onset course of Nup98 phospho-occupancy, NLS-reporter import, and TDP-43 localization; (ii) stress pulse–washout: if phosphorylation initiates, the phospho-signal should dissipate before import recovers; import failure persisting after phospho-loss supports a sequestration-first alternative and counters late-bystander phosphorylation.
• Perturbational test with graded predictions: a CRISPR multi-site phospho-null panel (clustered Ala substitutions across the nominated GLFG cluster), interpreted only after MS verification that candidate-site phospho-occupancy is suppressed. Outcome metric: NLS-import decline normalized to SG burden and soluble importin availability, quantified across mild-to-strong stress. Graded prediction: phospho-null neurons show a significantly attenuated early-phase import decline versus wild type at matched SG burden — not full preservation, because S4 establishes SG-independent-of-phosphorylation impairment. Late-phase failure in phospho-null neurons is expected and non-discriminating; only the early phosphorylation-attributable component counts. Interpretation rule: verified occupancy suppression plus an indistinguishable early normalized decline falsifies the hypothesis; failure to suppress occupancy (compensatory kinases/buffering) makes the test uninformative, not falsifying.
• Staged in vivo arm: only after in vitro discrimination, neuron-targeted multi-site Nup98 editing or kinase inhibition in a conditional TDP-43-mislocalization mouse, with import markers, TDP-43 localization, motor behavior, and survival as endpoints; post-mortem ALS tissue immunostained with the validated phospho-Nup98 reagent in neurons lacking cytoplasmic TDP-43 inclusions (early) versus affected neurons (late), as corroboration only.

Falsifying observation. With MS-verified suppression of the targeted Nup98 phospho-cluster (and no compensating phosphorylation at other mapped sites), mild stress produces an early-phase normalized import decline equal to wild type at matched SG burden and soluble importin availability; and in pulse–washout, import failure precedes or outlasts detectable Nup98 phosphorylation. Together these falsify initiating phosphorylation. Phosphomimetic results alone would not count toward falsification.

Limitations. Scoped to TDP-43-proteinopathy ALS; the S2 context is excluded. Packet evidence for pore involvement is associative; kinase identity, residues, and direction remain assumptions pending MS confirmation. Asp/Glu mimicry is weak, so gain-of-function relies on inducible kinase recruitment. Buffering is addressed only for the nominated cluster; broader nucleoporin compensation remains possible. iPSC and mouse models may not reproduce decades-long onset; post-mortem tissue is late-stage; phospho-signals are transient.

Final ranking:
1. Stress-activated phosphorylation of the FG-nucleoporin Nup98 initiates selective nuclear import failure upstream of TDP-43 mislocalization in TDP-43-proteinopathy motor neurons. (promisingness 0.46, confidence 0.62; PMIDs: 29311743, 26308891, 30853299, 29628143)

They recruited or mislocalized transport-associated proteins and were associated with impaired transport, nuclear TDP-43 depletion, and cell death. Phosphorylated TDP-43 accumulated in these assemblies. That is not itself evidence of nucleoporin phosphorylation. The experimental perturbations do not establish that every physiological ALS trajectory begins in this way.

## S4 — A stress-granule-associated route

Zhang et al. (2018), *Stress Granule Assembly Disrupts Nucleocytoplasmic Transport*. Cell. DOI: `10.1016/j.cell.2018.03.025`; PMID: `29628143`; PMCID: `PMC6083872`. [Primary record](https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/29628143/).

Cellular stress recruited transport factors into stress granules and impaired nucleocytoplasmic transport. Altering stress-granule assembly modified transport defects and disease-model phenotypes. This provides a sequestration-based alternative to an intrinsic pore-modification hypothesis. Read alongside S3, it does not justify assuming that conventional stress granules are required for every TDP-43-associated transport defect.

## Evidence boundaries

- These selected passages do not establish that nucleoporin phosphorylation initiates ALS. Label a proposed kinase, modification site, or interaction as an assumption unless a supplied source supports it.
- Specify the ALS context; do not assume a universal mechanism across genetic and sporadic disease.
- Distinguish pore alteration, transport-factor sequestration, and failure secondary to broader stress.
- Explain temporal and perturbational evidence that would distinguish cause from consequence.
- Propose a research hypothesis rather than claiming a mechanism or treatment has been validated.


Title: Stress-activated phosphorylation of the FG-nucleoporin Nup98 initiates selective nuclear import failure upstream of TDP-43 mislocalization in TDP-43-proteinopathy motor neurons.

Hypothesis. In sporadic ALS motor neurons whose dysfunction is driven by TDP-43 proteinopathy, sustained cellular stress activates a kinase that phosphorylates the FG-nucleoporin Nup98 at clustered Ser/Thr sites in or adjacent to its GLFG-repeat region. This phosphorylation increases pore passive permeability and lowers the rate of facilitated NLS-cargo import. The initiating lesion is an intrinsic pore modification; cytoplasmic TDP-43 de-mixing, transport-factor sequestration, Ran-gradient dissipation, and cell death follow as downstream amplifiers. C9orf72-repeat disease [S2] is excluded from this causal claim, although convergence at the level of import failure is permitted.

Causal chain, initiating versus downstream. Initiating: kinase activation → Nup98 GLFG-region phosphorylation → selective loss of facilitated NLS import and increased passive leak. Downstream: reduced nuclear retention of TDP-43 → cytoplasmic TDP-43 assemblies and phosphorylated TDP-43 accumulation [S3] → stress-granule formation and sequestration of import machinery [S4] → Ran-gradient collapse → cell death. The Ran gradient is deliberately decoupled from the initiation claim and used only as a downstream readout.

Supported premises. [S1] Nuclear-pore and transport components associate with insoluble TDP-43, and pore/transport pathology is present in ALS tissue — co-occurrence, not direction. [S3] Stress-granule-independent cytoplasmic TDP-43 assemblies impair import, deplete nuclear TDP-43, and recruit or mislocalize transport proteins — the downstream arm invoked here. [S4] Stress-granule assembly sequesters transport factors and impairs transport — the principal competing mechanism, and the reason perturbations must not rely on removing granules alone. [S2] Transport dysfunction exists in the C9orf72 genetic context and is used only to define scope. None of these sources identifies a nucleoporin phosphorylation event as causal.

Speculative bridges (assumptions, no packet support). A1: a stress-activated kinase (p38 or JNK as candidates) phosphorylates Nup98 in adult motor neurons. A2: the relevant residues are 2–3 clustered Ser/Thr sites near GLFG repeats, nominated from mitotic Nup98 phospho-mapping — this sourcing is unverified prior knowledge and must be re-confirmed by mass spectrometry before guiding construct design. A3: phosphorylation precedes TDP-43 egress; the packet only supports co-occurrence. A4: the mechanism is specific to TDP-43-proteinopathy ALS. Phosphomimetic Asp/Glu substitutions are acknowledged as chemically poor phosphate mimics and anchor no conclusion.

Discriminating preclinical test strategy. Model/context: human iPSC-derived motor neurons from sporadic ALS patients with TDP-43 pathology, with isogenic CRISPR-corrected controls; a parallel TDP-43-overexpression neuronal line as a convergent arm. Comparison arms: (i) stressed wild-type, (ii) stressed Nup98 knock-in phospho-null (S→A) at candidate residues, (iii) unstressed phosphomimetic knock-in, (iv) stressed cells expressing dominant-negative p38/JNK, (v) vehicle versus acute kinase-inhibitor additions. Measured outcomes: (a) time-resolved fluorescent NLS-cargo nuclear import rate per nucleus (primary discriminator), (b) baseline passive pore permeability by size-graded dextrans, (c) Nup98 phospho-occupancy at candidate residues by targeted mass spectrometry of immuno-purified pore fractions at hourly intervals, (d) nuclear/cytoplasmic TDP-43 ratio and cytoplasmic assembly burden by immunofluorescence, (e) importin-β and Ran sequestration into stress granules, (f) viability. Temporal precedence separates cause from consequence: the hypothesis predicts phospho-occupancy and import decline rise together and precede detectable cytoplasmic TDP-43 aggregation, whereas sequestration-first predicts import loss scales with granule number and importin sequestration regardless of Nup98 phospho-state.

Falsifying observation. The hypothesis is falsified in this model if (i) stressed Nup98 phospho-null knock-in motor neurons show NLS-import kinetics and nuclear TDP-43 retention indistinguishable from stressed wild-type — stress driving the same import loss without Nup98 phosphorylation and with no protection by the null allele, indicating sequestration or another pathway suffices; or (ii) Nup98 phospho-occupancy rises only after cytoplasmic TDP-43 assemblies are already detectable, reversing the claimed ordering and reclassifying phosphorylation as a consequence.

Limitations. Nup98 phosphorylation is proposed, not established, as an ALS cause; kinase identity and residues are assumptions. Phospho-null alleles may be functionally compensated by other pore components or modifications. iPSC-derived motor neurons may not reproduce adult late-onset biology, and line heterogeneity could obscure cell-specific timing. The claim is scoped to TDP-43-proteinopathy ALS and excludes universal extension to C9orf72 disease [S2], FTD, or all sporadic subgroups.

Argument for the top-ranked item: the packet establishes pore/transport disruption in ALS tissue and two candidate upstream-looking mechanisms [S3] [S4] but leaves direction unresolved. Selecting an intrinsic pore modification as the initiator is the most decisive divergence from sequestration-first alternatives, because a single site-level knock-in plus hourly phospho-mapping can dissociate pore chemistry from granule biology within one experiment. The evidence base is genuine yet incomplete, so promisingness and confidence are kept moderate.

Final ranking:
1. Stress-activated phosphorylation of the FG-nucleoporin Nup98 initiates selective nuclear import failure upstream of TDP-43 mislocalization in TDP-43-proteinopathy motor neurons. (promisingness 0.46, confidence 0.62; PMIDs: 29311743, 26308891, 30853299, 29628143)
